text:
Elaine: Quick follow-up on the tight-window handoff RFC — trying to nail operator UX for deferred apply across air-gapped nodes. We need a clear failure/retry surface and a simple mental model for operators. Any strong opinions on explicit resume tokens vs implicit idempotent steps?

Raj: I lean explicit tokens. In air-gapped flows we can't rely on ephemeral operator state. A token written to disk that the operator can present on resume makes audits easier.

Tom: +1 for tokens, but they complicate rotate/reuse. We should define lifecycle: token created at download end, rotated after successful apply-commit, and expired after X days.

Mina: UX concern: operators will copy manifests by thumbdrive, or we might seed a node through a seed bundle. If tokens are per-node, copying manifests needs a way to clear/claim tokens. Suggest a `claim-token` step in the operator CLI.

Elaine: Good point. Proposed flow:
1) bootstrap writes a `harvest` token during seed extract
2) operator runs `claim` to bind token to node identity (node-id + hw-fingerprint)
3) manifest apply produces a `resume` token after each safe checkpoint
4) if interrupted, operator presents `resume` token to resume apply

Tom: That handles copy-vs-claim. What about power-loss mid-chunk? We need very small checkpoints and an atomic journal entry so reboots are safe.

Raj: Agree. Implementation detail: keep checkpoints at component boundaries (e.g., model shard file, service unit). After chunk extract we write an atomic file marker `apply-<component>-done`. On restart we scan markers to pick next component.

Mina: Would like a CLI example we can hand to on-call and SRE for experiments. Something terse.

Elaine: Draft CLI snippet:

```
# download & claim
rwctl download --bundle /media/usb/bundle.tar.gz --out /var/lib/rw && \
rwctl claim --token /var/lib/rw/harvest.token --node-id $(cat /etc/rw/node-id)

# resume safely
rwctl resume --token /var/run/rw/resume.token --apply-dir /var/lib/rw
```

Raj: That looks fine. Add a `--force-verify` flag that rechecks signatures for the components you're about to resume, in case the thumbdrive was modified between steps.

Elaine: Good call. Also thinking about space-bounded verification: full verification of every blob is expensive on low-disk nodes. Option: incremental verify using the manifest merkle tree and streaming verify as we write. That avoids a second read pass.

Tom: Streaming verify + rolling hash is the right perf tradeoff. Also record per-blob hash in the journal so if resume happens we don't rehash already-committed blobs.

Mina: What about operator visibility? We should expose `rwctl show-journal` and a compact status endpoint that returns `applied: [components], pending: [components], last_error: "..."`. Operators will prefer a single-line human-friendly status.

Elaine: Agreed — add `--human` and `--json` modes. For automation, the controller uses JSON, human uses compact text.

Raj: One more safety net: automatic fallback to full-image swap if apply fails N times. That gives a known-good higher-latency path. But we need a policy: attempt in-place apply up to 3 times with backoff, then full-swap if available.

Tom: Policy sounds fine. Logging/telemetry must capture failure reasons so we can tune which components are flaky. Keep logs minimal on air-gapped nodes (rotate to /var/log/rw/).

Mina: Concern about token leakage: if a token is exfiltrated with a bundle, a malicious operator could replay resume. Mitigation: bind token to node-id and include a short-lived nonce during claim that requires node-local private key to sign.

Elaine: Summary action items:
- Define token lifecycle and claim API (Raj)
- Journal format (atomic markers + compact applied list) and CLI spec (Tom)
- Streaming verify design + hash metadata to avoid double reads (Mina)
- Fallback policy draft and metrics list (Elaine)

deploy-bot: Deployment checklist created: rfc/tight-window/hand-off-checklist.md (PR incoming) :white_check_mark:

Raj: I'll start drafting token RFC section with diagrams showing claim vs resume paths. Will include the signed nonce approach.

Tom: I'll prototype a journal layout and a small go utility to simulate powercut recovery.

Mina: I'll write the streaming-verify pseudo-code and perf targets for 4GB/8GB disks.

Elaine: Great — let's sync after the PRs land. If anyone hits an implementation constraint, call it out early — we should avoid coupling too many operator steps in the happy path. :thumbsup:
